D: Barry Allen goes back in time to save his mum and breaks the timeline.
P: Serve the mains when Barry's mum sends Henry out for a can of tomatoes.
S: Bacon, fried egg and cheddar in toasted English muffins
Toasted English muffins filled with a fried egg, crisp bacon and melted cheddar, wrapped in paper to eat on the run.
Popcorn tossed in lime zest, chilli flakes and melted butter
Popcorn tossed with butter and a pinch of chilli and lime, ready in a flash.
Wayne Manor baked brie with quince
Barry at the manor: "Are you in?"

A wheel of brie baked until runny, topped with warm quince paste, thyme and toasted walnuts, served with crackers and red grapes. Score the top of a 200g brie and sit it in a small baking dish. Warm 80g quince paste with 1 tbsp water in a small pan until spoonable. Bake the brie at 180C for 12 minutes until soft in the middle. Spoon the quince over, scatter with thyme leaves and 40g toasted walnuts and drizzle with a little honey. Serve straight away with 200g crackers and a bunch of red grapes.
M: Slow simmered tomato sauce with basil, tossed through spaghetti
Crushed tomatoes simmered with garlic, onion and basil for 45 minutes, tossed through spaghetti with parmesan.
Allen family lemon thyme roast chicken
dinner at the Allen family home

Chicken rubbed with butter, lemon and thyme, roasted at 200C for 75 minutes, with roast potatoes, peas and a pan gravy. Mix 40g soft butter with lemon zest and thyme and rub over a 1.8kg chicken. Put the zested lemon inside and roast at 200C for 75 minutes. Parboil 1kg potatoes in chunks for 8 minutes, rough them up and roast in hot oil alongside for 50 minutes. Rest the chicken 10 minutes. Stir 1 tbsp plain flour into the pan juices, whisk in 300ml chicken stock and simmer into gravy. Serve with buttered peas.
W: Fudgy dark chocolate brownies piped with a yellow bolt
Fudgy chocolate brownies baked at 170C for 25 minutes, cooled and piped with a yellow icing lightning bolt on each square.
K: Central City blood orange lightning fizz
Blood orange juice and honey ginger syrup in a salt rimmed glass

Blood orange and lime juice shaken with a ginger honey syrup, topped with sparkling water over crushed ice and a sugar-salt rim. Simmer 3 tbsp honey with 3 tbsp water and 1 tbsp grated ginger for 2 minutes, then cool and strain. Mix 1 tbsp caster sugar with a pinch of salt on a saucer, wet the rims of 4 glasses with lime and dip them in. Fill with crushed ice. Mix 400ml blood orange juice with the juice of 2 limes and the ginger syrup, pour into the glasses and top each with 80ml sparkling water.

s.note: Bacon, fried egg and cheddar in toasted English muffins
s.how: Fry 4 rashers of bacon until crisp and fry 4 eggs until just set. Split and toast 4 English muffins and butter them. Fill each with bacon, an egg and a slice of cheddar, then wrap tightly in paper so the cheese melts on the way.

s.note: Popcorn tossed in lime zest, chilli flakes and melted butter
s.how: Pop 100g popping corn in a big lidded pot. Melt 60g butter with the zest of a lime and a pinch of chilli flakes. Pour over the popcorn while tossing hard so every piece is coated, then squeeze over a little lime juice and serve straight away.

m.note: Slow simmered tomato sauce with basil, tossed through spaghetti
m.how: Soften a diced onion and crushed garlic in olive oil. Add 2 cans crushed tomatoes and simmer gently for 45 minutes. Stir in torn basil and season. Toss through 500g cooked spaghetti and finish with grated parmesan, just like the family kitchen.

w.note: Fudgy dark chocolate brownies piped with a yellow bolt
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate with 150g butter, whisk in 250g sugar and 3 eggs, then fold in 100g flour. Bake at 170C for 25 minutes and cool. Cut into squares and pipe a yellow lightning bolt of icing sugar mixed with a drop of colouring on each.
